about: After being nourished by the saving sacrifice, the community asks, through Augustine’s intercession, that the same sacrifice may be continually offered to God’s name in every place.

s01.translation: Lord, nourished by the saving sacrifice, we humbly entreat You that, through blessed Augustine’s intercession, this same sacrifice may be continually offered to Your name in every place. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever.

w003.explanation: The praying community has been nourished by the saving sacrifice and now entreats God. Hostia is the source of nourishment, not the subject doing the entreating.

w009.explanation: Eadem resumes the same hostia as the subject of the desired sacrificial offering. Its feminine singular form refers to that sacrifice, not to a new collection of gifts.

w011.explanation: The intercession belongs to Augustine of Canterbury, honored on May 28. The shared name does not identify him with Monica’s son Augustine of Hippo.

w012.explanation: The intercession is what intervenes, and blessed Augustine is its possessor. In English, through blessed Augustine’s intercession expresses the same relationship.

w020.explanation: The request concerns continual sacrificial offering to God’s name in every place. The passive verb does not identify a particular earthly celebrant.
